**Brazilian side**

- The apartment is subject to the **ITCMD** transfer tax, which can run up to **8 %** of the property’s value【1】.  
- Brazilian succession law forces **at least 50 % of the estate (the legitima)** to go to compulsory heirs—spouse, children, parents—regardless of where those heirs live【2】.  
- If you leave a will that tries to deviate from that 50 % rule, you’ll still have to comply with the same legal conditions that apply to Brazilian citizens【1】.

**U.S. side**

- Your U.S. accounts are **not touched by Brazilian inheritance rules**. They remain subject to U.S. estate‑tax rules.

- The Brazilian property does **not** trigger U.S. estate tax unless it’s also considered a U.S. asset (e.g., a U.S.‑situs property).

answer_raw:
Your Brazilian apartment will be handled under Brazilian succession law, while any U.S. bank accounts remain governed by U.S. rules.

**Brazilian side**  
The apartment is subject to Brazil’s **ITCMD** transfer tax, which can reach **8 %** of the property’s value【1】.  
Brazilian law imposes a **legítima** (forced heirship) of **at least 50 %** of the Brazilian‑situated estate that must go to compulsory heirs—spouse, children, parents—regardless of where those heirs live【2】.  
That 50 % rule applies only to the portion of the estate that is located in Brazil, not to the entire global estate.  
After the death, the heirs must initiate a formal **inventário** (inheritance inventory) in Brazil; the type of inventory (judicial or extrajudicial) determines the procedures and timelines, and failure to complete it can delay the transfer of the property.

**U.S. side**  
Your U.S. accounts are **not affected by Brazilian inheritance rules**. They stay under U.S. estate‑tax law.  
If the combined value of your U.S.‑situated assets (including any taxable gifts) exceeds **$60 k** at death, the executor must file **Form 706‑NA**【7】.  
The Brazilian apartment does **not** trigger U.S. estate tax unless it is also considered a U.S. asset, which it is not.

**What your heirs in the U.S. face**  
- If they inherit the Brazilian apartment, they will be subject to Brazil’s ITCMD and the 50 % forced‑heirship rule.  
- Their U.S. accounts will be taxed only under U.S. estate‑tax rules, and no Brazilian inheritance tax applies to those assets.  
- There is no publicly cited double‑taxation treaty that would alter this outcome, so the two jurisdictions apply independently.
